gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured latency for any HDMI-over-Cat6 transport; the only named measurement found is SC&T's own 100 m 4K60 test, which recorded under 1 ms for HDBaseT 3.0, about 40 ms for 1G SwiftSync and 40–300 ms for an H.265 extender. It did not test any candidate kit.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited OREI help-center pages (UHD12-EX115-K and UHD14-EXB400-K) and checked the other OREI support results by title. The cited pages give rated distances, 18 Gbps bandwidth and power draw (8.28 W and 35 W), but no latency figure and no measured result of any kind. The SC&T latency numbers are therefore new to the shopper. They are weak, though: a maker that sells all three technologies ran the test on its own hardware. No candidate kit was tested and no independent lab took part, so this does little to set a Dealectric page apart.
decides: It does not change the pick. At most it supports one general point. HDBaseT kits such as the OREI UHD14-EXB400-K send uncompressed video and add negligible delay (SC&T measured under 1 ms for HDBaseT 3.0, and the OREI kit's HDBaseT version wasn't confirmed). Compressed H.265 'over IP' extenders can add 40–300 ms, which matters for gaming or lip-sync. No source tested the OREI UHD12-EX115-K, the J-Tech JTECH-14EX60-AE or the OREI UHD14-EXB400-K, so no measurement separates the three candidates.

findings.label: Measured latency, 4K60 over 100 m of CAT cable
findings.source_title: HDBaseT vs H.265 vs SwiftSync: 4K HDMI Extender Latency Comparison
findings.note: Test by Smart Cabling & Transmission Corp. (SC&T), dated 2025-10-22, which makes and sells the products tested. Setup: a PC sending 4K60 into an HDMI splitter feeding three extenders on 100 m runs. A quad-view matrix showed the outputs, and a 4K capture box recorded them against on-screen millisecond timers, with mouse and window-drag tests. Not a candidate product.

Searches turned up no review of these kits from any of those outlets.

A measured maximum working distance at 4K60 over Cat6 for any candidate kit. OREI publishes only rated distances: 115 ft for the UHD12-EX115-K and 394 ft for the UHD14-EXB400-K. Retailer listings give 196 ft for the J-Tech, but I didn't open J-Tech's own product page.
Measured power draw or heat for any candidate kit. OREI states only the rated maximums: 8.28 W for the UHD12-EX115-K and 35 W for the UHD14-EXB400-K.
Whether the J-Tech JTECH-14EX60-AE compresses video (it's sold as 'over Ethernet'). Retailer listings don't say, and I didn't open J-Tech's spec sheet.
Which HDBaseT version the OREI UHD14-EXB400-K uses. I didn't open its spec sheet, so the SC&T HDBaseT 3.0 figure can't be applied to it directly.
